newsitem.title: USA: Entergy says still sees fy EPS $2.50-$2.55.
newsitem.headline: Entergy says still sees fy EPS $2.50-$2.55.

text.p: Entergy Corp said Thursday it still believes full-year earnings per share will be in the $2.50-$2.55 range.

"First quarter results show that our diversified growth businesses have become strong contributors to our bottom line results," said Gerald McInvale, Entergy's executive vice president and chief financial officer. "We are making good progress at implementing our business strategies."
Invale added that while it is too early to reliably forecast year-end earnings, he still believes full year earnings per share in the $2.50 to $2.55 range remain in focus.
Invale also said that because London Electricity's final capital structure is not yet determined Entergy's year-end earnings estimates do not currently take account of London Electricity.
"We will comment further on our earnings outlook as the year progresses," McInvale said.

Entergy said Thursday its first quarter consolidated net income rose to $109.8 million, or 47 cents per share, compared with a first quarter 1996 consolidated net loss of $87.1 million. The loss recorded in the comparable 1996 quarter was due to a $174.4 million after-tax write-off of deferred River Bend nuclear plant charges required by a change in accounting rules.

The company said when unusual items are eliminated, first quarter 1997's ongoing net income of $109.9 million and 47 cents per share compares with first quarter 1996's ongoing net income of $87.3 million and 38 cents per share. The 1997 quarter represents an increase of 25.9 percent in ongoing net income and a 23.7 percent increase in ongoing earnings per share.
